title: Boreal Systems - private deploy strategy & terraform module notes (draft)
content:
Context and goal

This is a working-strategy doc for a Boreal Systems private deployment (VPC + on-prem inference cluster) to support their realtime command-and-control assistant (alerts, routing, downstream recommendations). Customer target: 99th %-tile latency under 120ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens) and throughput of ~2k concurrent low-latency sessions during peak (estimated by Boreal). Primary constraints: strict network isolation (no egress except to selected SaaS), customer-managed KMS, and a requirement for offline deployable packages for air-gapped staging.

High-level proposal (summary)
- Deployment model: Hybrid VPC with a customer-owned AWS account for core control plane networking + on-prem GPU cluster in Boreal data center for inference pods. Control plane (optional lightweight agent) will be allowed to call Redwood control plane for feature flags/fallback but all inference traffic remains inside the VPC/on-prem fabric.
- Runtime sizing (initial): 6 inference nodes (each: 4x A5000-equivalent GPUs or 2x H100-smi) configured as 12x concurrent LLM worker processes per GPU using quantized 4-bit weights for the 13B model family (we recommend a quantized Llama-derivative at first). Expected steady-state QPS: ~1.2k (batched) with p95 latency ~90ms. Burst capacity: reserved spare CPU headroom for on-prem autoscaling by +2 nodes.
- Terraform approach: a modular repo split into network, infra (k8s nodepools), storage, secrets (KMS config), and redwood-runtime module. Each module has a well-defined tfvars file and examples folder for "airgap" packaging.

Sizing assumptions (why these numbers)
- Typical session = 20 tokens generated per turn; average work per request is small because Boreal mostly does short structured responses.
- Using a quantized 13B gives ~5–7x lower memory footprint vs fp16 13B and allows 2–3x concurrency per GPU compared to fp16.
- We conservatively plan for 60% GPU utilization on p95 traffic to avoid latency cliffs.
- Networking: expect 25–40Mbps sustained per GPU under peak (KV cache warm state) for prompt + kv transfers.

Detailed terraform module notes (working checklist)
- modules/network-vpc: create customer VPC with explicit private subnets, EIP blacklist, and managed NAT disabled. Outputs: private_subnet_ids, route_table_ids.
- modules/k8s-nodepool: multiple nodepools by GPU type (a5000-pool, h100-pool). Nodepool autoscaler config via k8s-cluster-autoscaler helm chart with scale-down disabled during first 2 weeks.
- modules/nfs/kv-cache: NFS-backed shared KV cache for warm-start across pods. Use EC2-backed EFS or on-prem NFS with explicit mounts; ensure mount options use noexec,nosuid (security dev note).
- modules/kms-integration: terraform does not store keys. Use data sources to reference existing customer-managed KMS key ARNs; we create role-to-key bindings in IAM. Provide a small wrapper script to generate sealed-secrets when packaging for air-gapped installs.
- modules/monitoring: prometheus + grafana helm chart values with preconfigured dashboards (latency/token-rate/cost-per-token). Export metrics to customer SAT (internal monitoring) via pull-proxy—don't send to Redwood by default.
- modules/redwood-runtime: public module that accepts model_profile (e.g., rwd-quant-13b), runtime_flags (enable_kv_cache:true, dynamic_batching:medium), and fallback_routes (hosted-api:disabled). This module produces CRs for redwood-runtime controller and a set of service accounts.

TF best-practices / gotchas
- Provider pinning: lock aws provider to ~> 5.15 and kubernetes provider to 2.14.x for cluster we tested.
- State locking: remote state in customer S3 with DynamoDB lock table; provide a helper script for state import during airgap.
- Secrets: do NOT store service tokens in plain tfvars; use terraform-cloud or remote state encrypted with SSE-KMS. For airgapped installs we produce sealedsecret yamls.

Architecture Q&A (customer-facing items to resolve)
Q: Do you require telemetry to Redwood control plane?
A: Boreal requested no telemetry beyond anonymized crash reports. We propose a minimal agent that only performs license checks and rollout flags; they can opt-out. Need final sign-off from security.

Q: What is the fallback model if an on-prem node fails?
A: Two options: 1) failover to a replica on-prem node pool (preferred), 2) fallback to Redwood-hosted model (requires egress allowance and contract). Recommend option 1 during initial rollout.

Q: Are GPU drivers and CUDA versions constrained?
A: Customer runs CUDA 12.x; we validated runtime images for CUDA 12.2 and 11.8. Recommend standardizing on 12.2 for H100 compatibility. Add a preflight script to test nvml visibility and nvidia-smi responses.

Upgrade and cutover plan (high level)
- Phase 0: Preflight (2–4 days)
  - Validate network routes, private DNS, and KMS bindings. Run container image pull tests from the airgap registry.
  - Run sample quantized model on 1 GPU to validate inference path.
- Phase 1: Initial deploy (3 days)
  - Provision nodepool: a5000-pool (2 nodes) + h100-pool (1 node, optional). Deploy runtime with conservative concurrency limits.
  - Smoke tests: synthetic latency and throughput tests (scripts in repo).
- Phase 2: Controlled ramp (1 week)
  - Gradually increase traffic via traffic-split (customer load generator). Monitor latency, memory pressure, error rates. Keep scale-down disabled.
- Phase 3: Live cutover (weekend window if desired)
  - Switch production DNS/ingress to on-prem gateway. Keep hosted fallback for 48 hours. Confirm metrics and rollback plan.
- Post-cutover (2 weeks)
  - Lower autoscaler thresholds, enable scale-down, adjust batching parameters. Run a model-quality smoke check against benchmarks.

Rollback considerations
- Keep hosted model credentials frozen and a pre-warmed hosted instance available. Rollback is: switch DNS back, scale down on-prem, and terminate failed node pool. Must coordinate with Redwood Ops if hosted fallback is used (ticket: JIRA-PD-712).

Operational runbook snippets (quick)
- Node GPU OOM: drain pod, restart pod with lower max-concurrency, trigger node-surgery (reboot + driver reinstall).
- KV cache corruption: reinitialize namespace with provided cleanup script; accept small cold-start cost for 10–30 min.
- KMS failure (permission denied): ensure role CBC (cross-account role) has kms:Decrypt on the key id; rotate test key to confirm.

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm exact GPU SKU preference with Boreal (A5000 vs A10G vs H100) — cost/latency tradeoffs to model once chosen.
- Decide on on-prem NFS vs local SSD for KV cache (tradeoff: cold-start vs replication complexity).
- Security review sign-off for the minimal agent (license/flags) — need Boreal Infosec nod.
- Create airgap packaging script that emits a single tarball with helm charts + sealed-secrets + tfstate import helpers.

Appendix: quick commands and test vectors
- preflight.sh (local) - runs: curl private-registry/auth, docker load < images.tar, kubectl get nodes && nvidia-smi
- load test: k6 script + python harness in scripts/loadtests/peak-session-20tokens.py

Notes to self (informal)
- Lin: add diagram (network flow + fallback route) before customer review.
- Sofia: verify monitoring dashboards map to Boreal's internal SLI names.
- Ethan: package example tfvars for their staging region and attach to PR 487.

End of draft.

(Version history: started 2025-06-12 by Arjun; edits 2025-06-17 by Sofia; 2025-06-20 tuning of GPU counts by Ethan)
